contract.inventory_scope: Fixed tools registered by build_registry in a clean workspace. User custom tools are loaded dynamically from the active workspace and listed at runtime by custom_tool_list; their instance-specific schemas are not present in this repository snapshot.
contract.metadata_semantics: effects and data_egress are declarative descriptions only. They do not enforce policy, prevent generated Python from importing Pyto modules, or guarantee provider-side data handling.
contract.stable_id_rule: Capability IDs equal existing registry tool names and must remain stable across compatible contract versions.
contract.proposal_compatibility: Effects are declarative and IDs stable so future capability proposals can reference this schema without redefining it.
contract.idempotency_note: idempotent is true or false when the source supports that claim; null means unknown.
contract.device_evidence_rule: No entry is marked device-tested without a dated run-log record from a real Pyto installation.
contract.runtime_result_note: The current ToolResult wire format exposes content:string and is_error:boolean. Four-state transport semantics are contract vocabulary, not implemented normalization.

proposed_capability_mapping.note: workspace text files; not an arbitrary Files-provider path
not a model-facing tool; device_capabilities reports availability but does not return location
keepalive_start is not a general scheduler
text share sheet, not arbitrary typed app intents

capabilities.summary: Look up Pyto's own bundled modules and what Pyto does not have. Call this BEFORE writing a program that imports a Pyto module: with no argument it lists the modules available on this device plus everything Pyto lacks (Reminders, HealthKit, Bluetooth, speech recognition, pip install of C extensions, a daemon); with module='photos' it gives that module's real members, signatures, a minimal snippet and caveats. Pyto's API is small, version-specific and easy to misremember, so use only the members it reports. If run_program raises AttributeError/ImportError about a Pyto module, call this again for that module instead of guessing a second name.

module.description: A Pyto module, e.g. 'pasteboard', 'photos', 'pyto_ui'. Empty lists them all.

member.description: Optional: narrow one module to a single member, e.g. 'set_string'.

capabilities.summary: Run a Python program and return its stdout/stderr. Pass a workspace path, or raw source to try something once. Use this to test what you wrote before telling the user it works. Keep programs short and non-blocking: Pyto runs them inside this app, and Python cannot interrupt a program blocked in a native call. A surviving run holds the execution lane until it exits.

path_or_source.description: A workspace-relative .py path, or inline Python source.

args.description: Command-line arguments passed to the program.

timeout_s.description: Requested runtime before timeout (default 30, max 300). Pyto allows a short unwind grace; code blocked in native code or a child thread may remain active. Desktop child processes can be killed.

input_values.description: Validated values for a registered program's input_schema. Input-enabled entry files implement def main(inputs); use test values when verifying one.

capabilities.summary: Change this harness's own source. Prefer the smallest change: pass old_string/new_string for a surgical patch, or new_source for a whole (small) file. The change is written, then a bounded slice of the offline test suite runs (the modules that cover the file, a few seconds): kept only if it passes, otherwise the previous bytes are restored and you are told exactly why. Read the file with read_source first, and run selftest before editing. Pass full_tests=true only when the change is broad enough to need the whole suite. Do not use this to work around a missing iOS permission: report the user action instead.

new_source.description: The complete new file (omit when patching).

reason.description: One line: what problem this fixes.

full_tests.description: Gate on the whole suite instead of the covering subset (slower).

capabilities.summary: Ask iOS to run an exactly named Shortcut via x-callback-url and request a callback to Pyto. Current harness code ignores the return value from xcallback.open_url; a successful ToolResult means the URL handoff was requested, not that the Shortcut's semantic result was received.

input_text.description: Optional text handed to the Shortcut.

output_schema.description: Current model-visible text says the URL was handed to iOS and states the callback URL. The callback's result is not captured by this handler.

transport.state_encoding: draft normalization. Current wrapper returns ToolResult success/error for the handoff; xcallback exceptions fall back to open_url, and SystemExit/cancellation may escape. The registry timeout does not kill a blocked worker.

semantic_result.shortcut_output: not captured by current harness handler; Pyto's xcallback documentation describes a returned string, but the handler discards the call's return value.
semantic_result.semantic_failure: a normal returned text value is semantically opaque; harness cannot infer that the Shortcut's business operation succeeded.
semantic_result.transport_ok_means: the URL handoff was accepted by the selected opener, not that the Shortcut ran or returned.

declared_destinations: the exactly named user Shortcut (contents and side effects unknown)

prerequisites: Pyto xcallback bridge or URL opener available
capabilities.foreground_requirement: unknown; requires an iOS URL handoff and actual behavior must be measured on device
capabilities.reversible: unknown; entirely dependent on the user-authored Shortcut
capabilities.latency_class: 30-second registry wait limit; actual xcallback duration and post-timeout worker lifetime are unverified

limits.max_input_bytes: unknown until A13 is run on a real Pyto installation
limits.max_output_bytes: unknown until A5 is run on a real Pyto installation
limits.name_resolution_and_encoding: unknown until A14-A17 are run on a real Pyto installation
limits.return_value_behavior: Source-verified: the registered wrapper discards the opener return value. A direct xcallback.open_url call returned str in device case A20 on 2026-10-07; other return, encoding, and size behaviors remain unknown.
limits.recovery: unknown until A6-A8 are run on a real Pyto installation

examples.note: Illustrative only; use a fixture the user created and explicitly confirmed.

evidence.device_status: partial: direct xcallback A20 observed on a real Pyto installation; registered shortcut_run_wait handler not exercised end-to-end

runtime.pyto_app_version: unknown; no stable stdlib API exposes it

device_observations.scope_note: Direct xcallback test only; does not test the registered handler, which discards the callback return value.
